content.intro: This lesson covers AutoFill and the Fill Handle as part of Data Entry and Cell Management. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: AutoFill and the Fill Handle establishes the workbook structure and data-quality habits that later formulas and reports depend on. A clear layout reduces avoidable editing mistakes and makes the workbook easier for another person to understand. Compatibility: Check Microsoft’s function reference for the target Excel version, platform, and update channel. Dynamic-array spill behavior and some newer functions are not available in every legacy installation.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: AutoFill and the Fill Handle focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: Copying values and formulas; Filling sequences; Completing date and number series; Custom lists and Fill Series. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.expected_output: Calculates a date/time result using serial values; the exact interpretation depends on cell values, formatting, locale and whether holidays or overnight intervals matter.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Enter real Excel date/time values, not ambiguous text. Apply an appropriate number format and test boundaries such as month-end, blanks and overnight durations.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a small, known dataset for autofill and the fill handle. Apply the example above, compute or inspect at least one result independently, then deliberately try a blank, duplicate, boundary, or not-found case where relevant.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates autofill and the fill handle. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.
